title: The match consequence that rwb-treatment consumes is not published, and no source names the plan states the treatment row holds after a match
source: Legacy RWB-E2-027 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 027 Payment matching rules with the data team v2.md, sections 4, 7, 11, 12 and 13); FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A2.10.3.1, A2.11.3.1, A2.12.3.1; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T2, T3.0, T3.1, T5.2, T5.3 and appendix T-A.2; _work/msr/context/S2.md (ownership rows: tables 1 treatment, jobs 0, events 1 EV-10, workflows 1 TreatmentWorkflow); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11 and R7.2 section 12; _work/msr/fragments/RWB-P8-E2027-CON.json
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5; 8 Business rules BR1 and BR3; 11 Data; 12.2; 12.8; 13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the S2 to P8 boundary. (1) The legacy story consumed the match inside one module through RuleEvaluator, the rule_row table and TreatmentApi.recordInstallmentPaid; after the split the treatment side must read the consequence from rwb-payment, and no source publishes the operation, its path, its response media type or its payload members: TSD S2 T5.2 states only that calls go through the published interfaces of P3, P4, P5, P6 and P7, and names no payment interface. (2) No source states how a matched or partially matched installment reaches rwb-treatment once the matching engine is rwb-payment's: the design names the missed-payment event EV-12 and the signal the case router passes to the stage workflow, and states nothing for a match whose installment was met in part. (3) No source names the plan states the treatment row carries: PLAN_RUNNING and PLAN_BROKEN appear in the FSD rule tables and PLAN_CURE_PERIOD only in the legacy story section 9, so the vocabulary of the state column is taken from those two places and not from a data dictionary entry. (4) No source gives field IDs to the match-consequence members, so section 11 cites the contract rather than the Logical Data Model.
evidence: TSD S2 v2 T5.2 ('Calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices') and T5.3 (one published event, TreatmentApproved); legacy RWB-E2-027 section 12 ('Published interfaces called': RuleEvaluator.evaluate, RuleCatalog.row, DecisionLogApi.write, TreatmentApi.recordInstallmentPaid) and section 13 ('folder recovery/payments/matching'); FSD S2 v3 A2.10.3.1 (R-RES-25, PLAN_RUNNING) and A2.11.3.1 (R-RES-29, R-RES-30); legacy section 9 (PLAN_CURE_PERIOD, R-RES-28); _work/msr/context/S2.md (Tables (1) treatment; Events (1) EV-10; Workflows (1) TreatmentWorkflow)
area: S2 to P8 contract for the treatment side of a payment match
owner_role: Contract owner of rwb-treatment with the owner of rwb-payment and the solution architect
proposed: Publish one read in RWB-P8-E2027-CON that returns, for a case, a plan and a business date, the payment code, the installment due date, the match type, the rule ID, the package code and version and the shortfall; carry the plan states PLAN_RUNNING, PLAN_CURE_PERIOD, PLAN_BROKEN and BACK_TO_ROUTE_DECISION on the treatment state column as stated in section 9; name the payload members in the contract document at major version 1.

title: No source names the rule set, the parameter codes or the signal that announce a plan state change, and none states who consumes the plan consequence once rwb-treatment owns it
source: Legacy RWB-E2-027 sections 2, 8, 10 and 13; FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A2.11.3.1 (R-RES-29, R-RES-30, R-RES-31); TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T4, T5.2, T5.3 and T6.1; _work/msr/context/S2.md (naming and shared platform rules; architecture slide 9 note on R-RES-27 to R-RES-31 and restructure.max_breaks; slide 11 runtime view); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04, DP-06, DP-10 and DP-14; R3 default rulings (parameters and reference data owned by rwb-case, rule package registry owned by rwb-decision)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1, AC4, AC5, AC6; 8 Business rules BR5, BR6 and BR9; 12.2; 12.5; 12.8; 13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the rule and parameter side. (1) No source states which package code holds the RES rule set of the route, or whether the R-RES-25 to R-RES-31 rows are evaluated by rwb-treatment at all once the PAYMENT_MATCH rows stay with rwb-payment: the design names PAYMENT_MATCH, RESTRUCTURE and BOOKING_MATCH as the phase 1 packages, and the story needs to know which of them decides the plan consequence. (2) No source names the parameter codes that carry the cure period and the break limit: the design example gives 30 calendar days for MORTGAGE and restructure.max_breaks = 2 as values, and states no parameter key, no owner of a change and no version reference. (3) No source names the signal or event by which a plan state change is announced to the case and to reporting: TSD S2 T5.3 lists one published event, TreatmentApproved, and the legacy story raised no plan event, so a plan broken on the treatment row is read through the contract and not announced here. (4) The embedded Drools runtime and the client libraries of rwb-case are named by the DP table as platform and P3 contract stories, while the Work Package carries H empty and one contract dependency, so the build dependencies are carried as fakes (ASM-B2-S2-023-2).
evidence: Temporal and Drools Design slide 5 note via the context pack ('Only RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH and BOOKING_MATCH (S2) are named Drools packages in Phase 1'); context pack slide 9 ('R-RES-27 starts the cure period: 30 calendar days for MORTGAGE (CURE_PERIOD_DAYS)', 'restructure.max_breaks = 2'); TSD S2 v2 T4 (R-RES-01 to R-RES-25 listed, the rest in the Business Rules and Routing Logic workbook) and T5.3; FSD S2 v3 A2.11.3.1 (R-RES-29, R-RES-30); legacy RWB-E2-027 section 8 (BR5, BR10) and section 13 ('Feature flag rwb.payments.matching-rules')
area: Rule package, parameter and notification ownership across S2, P3 and P7
owner_role: Solution architect with the rule owner of rwb-decision and the parameters owner of rwb-case
proposed: Evaluate the RES rule set of the route in rwb-treatment with the package in force from rwb-decision, read CURE_PERIOD_DAYS and restructure.max_breaks from the parameters contract of rwb-case, publish no plan event in wave 2 and serve the plan consequence on the treatment read; treat the package code and the parameter keys as the open items of the contract freeze.
